summary: Authority push verifies the signed replica once per push session; backup pages carry only the manifest SHA. The master reports a degraded check at 80% of any backup authority limit. API impact: changed contract.

guide.reason: Operators now see the backup authority limits and the 80% capacity warning.

api.reason: POST /api/v1/pool/replica/backup-page no longer carries the signed replica on every page: index -1 with the replica opens a 10 minute push session, pages carry manifest_sha256 (project owner: no compatibility with the per-page protocol). Core adds the pool-backup-authority-capacity host check, degraded at 80% of a limit; it uses the existing checks list, so no Controller route changes.

roadmap.reason: Completes a deferred item of the existing backup authority slice.

state.reason: The session is in-memory member state and the usage measurement an in-memory cache; both rebuild from the next push or the next minute's measurement. No durable record is added.

verification.method: Focused Core tests over the real mTLS peer transport: one session open and small page requests for a large v2 authority, forged replica, unlisted page hash, foreign manifest and expired session refused, and the 80% check appearing and clearing. Existing authority, promotion and transfer tests rerun by focused regex.
verification.limits: Version-2 manifests carry only a full-stream root, so an unlisted version-2 page is caught by the final root check rather than on arrival. No lab, native host or forge CI run.
